title: Miro Business to self-hosted Excalidraw
summary: Excalidraw is a fraction of Miro and runs on almost nothing — but it is a whiteboard, not a workspace, and that distinction decides this one.

you_lose: Miro's templates, frameworks and the meeting facilitation tooling built on top of them
Infinite-canvas features like voting, timers and Jira integration
Comment threads and the review workflow around them
you_gain: A static front end that costs almost nothing to run and almost never breaks
Drawings stored as plain files you can version and diff
MIT licensing, the most permissive on this site

caveats: These are not the same product. Excalidraw is a sketching tool; Miro is a workspace people run meetings in. If your team lives in Miro, this comparison is not for you.
Real-time collaboration needs the separate excalidraw-room server. The estimate assumes you deploy both.
There is no Miro importer. Existing boards are recreated by hand or not at all.
